 LONDON, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 28: Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin and Ralph Fiennes speak onstage at “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” UK Fan screening event at HMV Westfield Shopping Centre on October 28, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Lionsgate UK) 
 By Pueng Vongs | pvongs@bayareanewsgroup.com | Bay Area News Group PUBLISHED: November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM PST | UPDATED: November 9, 2026 at 4:30 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is already a hot ticket in the South Bay — more than a week before its official opening day, on Friday, Nov. 20.
 Prime seats at popular local theaters are being snapped up quickly for the highly anticipated prequel, especially for high-demand showing times like the early screenings on Wednesday, Nov. 18.
 The storyline takes place 24 years before the events of the original trilogy, tracking the 50th Hunger Games. Box office reports indicate the film is outpacing last year’s massive debut of “Wicked: For Good.” It features A-list actors, including Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin and Ralph Fiennes, as well as appearances by original stars Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson.
 Booking tickets in advance is highly recommended for moviegoers looking to secure seating for premium formats like IMAX, Dolby Cinema and XD.
 Here is a snapshot of current availability at popular theaters across the South Bay:
 AMC Sunnyvale 12 
150 E. McKinley Ave, Sunnyvale
 The Nov. 18 screening in IMAX at 6 p.m. only has front-row seating remaining. However, some decent seats are still left in the Dolby Cinema format at 6:30 p.m.
 AMC Mercado 20 
3111 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara
 The Nov. 18 shows are selling out fast in the most popular premium formats: IMAX and Dolby Cinema. There are more seats left in 3D.

 Cinemark Century Oakridge 20
 925 Blossom Hill Rd, Suite 2000, San Jose
 Advance tickets for Nov. 18 premium XD and ScreenX formats are heavily booked and prime evening slots on opening weekend could sell out.
